name: cloud_normalise
description: Turn identified cloud log exports into canonical rows, offline, and keep everything an adapter cannot read. Input: CSV, JSON (an array, one object, or an envelope such as entries, items or value), JSON Lines and gzip of those, one file, several (paths) or directories of them; the format is read from the content. Three adapters read documented JSON shapes (fixtures are authored from the published field lists, not copied from a vendor page; no real export exists and the live documentation pages were not read while building them): gcp_audit reads a Cloud Logging LogEntry whose protoPayload is a google.cloud.audit.AuditLog (principal and its delegation chain, service, method, resource, status, caller address and user agent, insertId, timestamp against receiveTimestamp, the log type from logName, the monitored resource); kubernetes_audit reads audit.k8s.io/v1 Event records, alone, as JSON Lines or in an EventList (audit id, stage, level, verb, request URI, user, groups, impersonation, source addresses, object reference, response status, both timestamps, annotations): a record is one stage and one row, so the stages of one audit id are separate rows and are never merged into one action; entra_directory_audit reads a Microsoft Graph directoryAudit (id, category, correlation id, result and reason, activity, logging service, operation type, the initiator as user or application kept apart from the target resources, and each target's modified properties). Every row has: provider, adapter, tenant (a gcp project, organisation or folder; the Kubernetes and Entra records name none and the row says so), principal, action, resource, outcome (success, failure, or unknown when the record says nothing, with its basis), the raw time and the UTC time, a locator (file, record, line, offset in characters of the decoded text, which is the byte offset only for ASCII text), a duplicate annotation, the parser label and the whole record, cleaned. A time with no zone is never read as UTC: time_utc is null, time_status says no_zone and time_raw is kept; a day/month/year string is not guessed either. A record that parsed and that no adapter reads (for the requested provider), a malformed line, a truncated record and a record larger than max_record_bytes go to rejected.jsonl with the reason and the locator, and are counted in coverage as rejected, unsupported or malformed: none is dropped. Outputs, under out_dir (default: cloud-normalise under $OUT in a job, work/<agent>/cloud-normalise otherwise): normalised.jsonl (every row; the answer carries one page), rejected.jsonl and coverage.json (per source file: format, records read, rows, rejected, unsupported and malformed, the observed time range, pagination markers such as nextPageToken or @odata.nextLink, the first failures, and the status). A read that ended early or left anything out publishes normalised.partial.jsonl and coverage.partial.json; an output is never replaced by a smaller one, or by any other: a file already at an output name is kept (the new one is kept beside it as name.2.ext, or is the file when the bytes are equal). A duplicate (the same record id and stage seen again) is annotated and kept; nothing is deduplicated. Duplicates are annotated among the first 500000 distinct record keys, and the coverage says when the annotation stopped. `status` and `status_basis` say whether every record of the supplied files was read and turned into a row; complete says nothing about whether the export holds everything the provider logged (export completeness is not logging completeness). A file that names a next page (nextPageToken, @odata.nextLink) keeps the run partial. provider is auto (each record is given to the first adapter that recognises it) or one of gcp, kubernetes and entra (a record that is not that provider's is rejected, named). principal is a regex (at most 200 characters, a pattern of a known exponential shape is refused, every test is timed at a quarter of a second) matched against the principal as it is printed, never against a withheld original. One clock: time_limit_seconds (default 420, at most 480, the call allows 600) covers the listing of directories, the reading, the withholding and the writing of the rows; a run that reaches it is partial and names the files it did not read. A termination signal ends the run with a partial coverage file (coverage.partial.json), one line of JSON on stdout and exit 128 plus the signal. NOT measured: whether the provider logged everything, how long it kept it, whether the export holds all of what was logged, whether a principal was the person it names, or what a request did beyond what its record says. SENSITIVE: principal names, addresses and user agents are in the rows. Withholding is the shared block of every pack that withholds, with a 1 MiB gate here: identifiers (record, audit and correlation ids, project ids, object ids) are printed as they are; every other string goes through the credential rules only; a field named like a secret goes through the name layer. A Kubernetes request or response body that is a Secret object (an objectRef of secrets, or a body of kind Secret or SecretList) is replaced whole by a marker. The values of Entra modified properties are sensitive: a property whose name says password, secret, credential or token, or is named like a secret, has its old and new values withheld, and every other value goes through the credential rules. A field named or shaped like a credential is withheld and its original written only with write_values, in a job, to a mode 0600 file under $OUT: run as a job with secret_output: true when the case treats the export as sensitive. Known gaps: a secret with neither a credential name nor a token shape, and a Secret body that is neither under secrets nor of kind Secret, are printed; the Entra portal's own CSV layout and the Azure, S3 and VPC formats are not read by this version (their records are rejected and counted); a CSV is read only when its header carries the Graph property names; nothing is read from archives (.zip, tar: named, not read).

path.description: One export file or a directory of them (the files of a directory are read in name order, then its subdirectories)

paths.description: Several files or directories, read in the order given; a file listed twice is read once

provider.description: auto (default: each record goes to the first adapter that recognises it), gcp, kubernetes or entra; a record that is not the named provider's is rejected, named

format.description: auto (default: from the content), csv, json or jsonl; a file whose content contradicts it is not read and is listed as unsupported

delimiter.description: CSV delimiter, one character (default a comma)

out_dir.description: Directory for normalised.jsonl, rejected.jsonl and coverage.json, under the run directory (in a job, under $OUT: name it work/<your agent id>/..., which becomes $OUT). Default: cloud-normalise under $OUT in a job, work/<agent>/cloud-normalise otherwise. A file already at an output name is kept and the new one is named beside it

principal.description: Case-insensitive regex (at most 200 characters) over the principal as printed; only matching rows are written (the rest are counted in records_filtered_out); a pattern of a known exponential shape is refused, and every test is timed (a quarter of a second)

limit.description: Rows of each list returned inline (default 500, an inline page size); the whole is always in the files the answer names

max_expanded_bytes.description: Most bytes read from one file after decompression (default 4 GiB); a file that reaches it is partial and says so

max_record_bytes.description: Most text held while one record is read (default 16 MiB; a CSV line too); a larger record is rejected, located and listed, never cut (in an array or an envelope it is skipped by scanning to its end without holding it, and the records after it are read)

time_limit_seconds.description: Stop reading after this many seconds (default 420, at most 480, so the answer is written well inside the 600 seconds a call has); the limit is checked inside a record too; what was read is kept, the answer is partial and names the files not read

write_values.description: Write the originals of the values withheld from the answer to a mode 0600 file under $OUT. The manifest declares secret output for it: a job with write_values runs as secret output whether or not the agent set the flag, and its values file is sealed sensitive. Honoured only in a job whose SECRET_OUTPUT is 1; outside a job, or in a job that is not secret output, it is refused as JSON and nothing is written
